text:
The Indian market posted a strong week, with the Nifty 50 closing at 25,030.35, up 8.58 % and the Bank Nifty at 59,086, up 8.04 %. Broad‑based buying was evident – the breadth score was 67.3, labelled “HEALTHY”, with 71.2 % of stocks above their 20‑day moving average. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added INR 45,960 crore, extending an eight‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 24,196 crore, marking six consecutive days of net outflows. The volatility index (India VIX) fell to 17.47, down 14.15 % for the week, reflecting calmer market conditions.

In IPO activity, five listings debuted this week. BLS Polymers Limited showed the biggest first‑day jump, gaining 65.3 % and 57.2 % since issue, while SFC Environmental Technologies rose 7.6 % (25.2 % since issue). Bombay Coated and Special Steels gained 11.0 % (9.8 % since issue), M.K. Sons Fine Jewels added 5.6 % (‑2.4 % since issue), and EAAA India Alternatives edged up 0.6 % (1.0 % since issue). No new IPOs are scheduled for the coming week in the data set.

Looking ahead, the next week could be shaped by several factors. A weaker USD‑INR at 93.89 (‑1.32 % weekly) may support export‑linked stocks, while Brent crude’s 16.98 % drop to $97.66 could lift energy‑sensitive sectors. Internationally, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures fell 2.26 % and 4.36 % respectively, suggesting broader risk‑off sentiment. Domestically, the “LEADING” sector quadrant lists Financial Services, Consumption, Infrastructure, Realty and Auto as the strongest, whereas IT, Bank and Pharma are “WEAKENING”. Keep an eye on these macro cues and sector trends for next‑week market direction.
